versos.texto_bv: E Lia tinha os olhos baços; Raquel, porém, era formosa de porte e de aparência.
versos.traducao_literal: E os olhos de Lia tenros; e Raquel foi formosa de forma e formosa de aparência.
objecoes: Objeção MATERIAL (revisão ER-0019): BV traduz `rak` (רַכּוֹת) como 'baços' (opacos/sem brilho), divergindo das três referências: NTLH/NVIPT 'meigos' e ARA 'enfermos'. O léxico hebraico `rak` significa 'tenro, delicado, suave' — a correção para qualquer destes termos mudaria a interpretação do estado dos olhos de Lia. — evidência: Consenso das três referências (NTLH 'meigos', ARA 'enfermos', NVIPT 'meigos') contra 'baços' da BV. Léxico hebraico `rak` (H7390) = tenro, delicado. A substituição alteraria o sentido adotado pela BV.

kjv.texto: Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.

vizinhos.16: And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
vizinhos.18: And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.

web.texto: Leah’s eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and attractive.

vizinhos.16: Laban had two daughters. The name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
vizinhos.18: Jacob loved Rachel. He said, “I will serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.”
